feedback: Written before this candidate races. Race 5 (606.82) and race 6 (389.47) together show that the five-sensor layout at y = 0.06 with 16 mm footprints is the best platform. Race 6 was the seven-sensor density test: oval fell to 4/20, s-bend to 7/20, and slalom line loss rose to 1.25, so density is not the slalom limiter. Your decision to hold the race 5 geometry is supported. The controller is now tuned for slalom response (kp 3.2, kd 0.6, base_speed 0.95), so any change in slalom in the next race comes from gain and speed. Once the race reports: if slalom line loss falls below 1, keep the geometry and tell me which change to use. If slalom still loses the line at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06, the platform is limiting, so I will ask you for a geometry change with a clearer hypothesis.
requested_changes: Hold the race 5 geometry (five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.06, body 0.18 by 0.12, wheels 0.03 radius and 0.12 track, 0.8 kg) for the next race, so the gain and speed change is tested alone.

Do not move the lead further forward (y 0.065) unless oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.25 and oval finishes hold at 18 or more of 20, as your own rule requires. Race 4 showed the 0.05 to 0.06 move changed oscillation by only about 0.01.

Optional exploration only, if slalom still loses the line at 1 or more after this race: test wheel_track at the low end (0.10 m) with the same sensors. This is untested and would sharpen yaw response on tight bends, but it changes the turning dynamics and needs a controller rescale.
